title: Opening Remarks
How Technology is Reshaping Grocery: Perspectives from Instacart CEO Chris Rogers
takeaways: Instacart is positioning itself as an “operating system for grocery”: its storefront technology powers 380 grocery e-commerce sites, and retailers can take the full stack (e.g. Sprouts) or single modules (e.g. Kroger uses it for fulfilment only).
Affordability is the top barrier to online grocery. Retailers without online markups grow about 10 points faster on Instacart; Instacart+ offers $0 delivery from $10, plus pickup and no-rush options.

AI will transform grocery more than any other category: Clementine (consumer) and Cart Assistant (white label for retailers); integrations with Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini, but the best agentic experiences should live on owned channels.
New software turns the physical shelf into a real-time digital view; the retail media network keeps adding partners.
transcript_note: The recording starts partway through the first answer.

title: Kroger's Approach to Harnessing and Scaling AI
takeaways: AI's biggest omnichannel impact is removing the seam between digital and physical: customers have needs and occasions, not channels.
Principles before deploying AI: prove customer value first, ground it in trusted first-party data, keep a human in the loop; the data layer is the one thing not to compromise.
An internal AI gateway orchestrates Kroger's own models alongside frontier-model partners, keeping flexibility rather than picking a winner.
The AI shopping assistant builds baskets from context such as handwritten recipes; adoption is spread across all customer segments and baskets are larger, not smaller.
Behind the shelf, replenishment is autonomous; every associate can get an “AI driver's license”.

title: Title TBC: Grocery ecommerce fulfillment session
title_note: Title, date, time and stage not shown in the screenshot; the About text begins “Grocery ecommerce is seeing significant growth, yet fulfillment and delivery costs continue to hinder profitability.”
takeaways: AlixPartners: grocers' omnichannel share keeps rising while earnings fall; same-day delivery is table stakes, and cost is the top concern for fulfilment executives.
Migros (online since 1997, about 23% online share) never offered free delivery and reached e-commerce profitability after six loss-making years; about 60% of orders are ultra-fast (under 30 minutes).
Picking-cost levers at Migros: bonus structures, store layout and back-room mini dark stores, pick-to-light and cobots; biggest wish is ending items stuck in the back room.
Mercado Libre measures grocery on customer lifetime value across categories; robotics lifted picking productivity by 300%; biggest wish is better inventory placement.

title: How DoorDash Crafts AI-Powered Shopping Experiences
speakers_note: The app shows Zia Daniell Wigder’s title and organisation in swapped fields (“Hyve Group” as title); they are shown here in the usual columns.
takeaways: Costco is now on DoorDash, bringing all top-10 US grocers to the platform; SNAP/EBT is supported at over 75,000 stores.
Ask DoorDash (launched June): about 50% larger grocery carts, 5x faster checkout and 60% more unique items versus non-AI orders, with cross-store inventory checks.
Retailers' no-regrets move is clean catalogue and inventory data; Dasher shelf photos feed back to retailers, and a new Brand Center gives brands stock and performance data.
AI should make purchasing more frictionless, not take the decision away from the customer.

title: Beyond Category Lines: How Unilever Serves the New Wellbeing Consumer
takeaways: Three shifts drove Unilever Wellbeing: health as a lifestyle, the convergence of beauty and wellbeing, and the digitisation of everything.
The portfolio is about 50/50 online and in store; Unilever ran 17 clinical studies in 2025 and sees LLMs as a way to make that science accessible.
Physical retail still matters: more than half of shoppers prefer to discover products in store, so retailer partnerships stay critical.

title: Track Keynote: Building a Continuous, End-to-End Supply Chain
takeaways: BJ's created a Chief Supply Chain Officer role that unifies planning, allocation, distribution, logistics and automation around availability, convenience and value for members.
One metric matters most: on-shelf availability at the moment the member wants to buy.
AI approach is “continuous and end to end”, moving towards a self-healing supply chain; shelf-scan data becomes task lists for club leaders, and planners query AI in plain language.
Adoption is staged (assist, then human-monitored, then agents working together), starting with simple use cases to build trust.

title: How Sam's Club Resonates with Consumers Demanding Value
takeaways: Sam's Club defines value as a quality item worth the price, delivered in a way only Sam's can, with the same prices online and in club.
Myron Frazier uses a decades-old document from the Walmart archives on what makes a good Sam's Club item as a rubric for merchants (e.g. the item should sell itself).
Member's Mark is shaped with a member community of 200,000+ people generating around 200,000 activities a month; organics doubled and will double again.
Advice for suppliers: be clear on the value you offer and listen to member feedback.
